chunks: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) went out during a night in which it had drizzled, and he was intending to go to the canopy of the Banu Sa'ida. So I followed him, and there was something that had fallen from him, and he said: 'In the name of God; O God, return it to us.' Then I came to him and greeted him. Then he said: 'Mu'alla?' I said: 'Yes, may I be your ransom.' So he said to me: 'Search with your hand, and whatever you find, hand it over to me.' So I found a great deal of scattered bread, and I kept handing him whatever I found. Then I was faced with a sack of bread that I was unable to carry. So I said: 'May I be your ransom! Let me carry it on my head.' He said: 'No, I have more right to it than you. But come along with me.'

He said: So we came to the canopy of Banu Sa'ida, and we found a group of people sleeping there. He went on tucking the bread — one loaf and two loaves — until he reached the last of them. Then we left. So I said: 'May I be your ransom! Do these people know the truth?' He said: 'If they had known it, we would have shared with them the fine seasoning — and the fine seasoning is salt.'

Indeed, God, Blessed and Exalted, has not created anything except that it has a treasurer who stores it — except for charity, for the Lord attends to it Himself. And my father, when he gave something in charity, would place it in the hand of the beggar, then take it back from him, kiss it and smell it, then return it to the hand of the beggar. A charity given at night extinguishes the anger of the Lord, erases great sin, and eases the reckoning. And a charity given by day yields wealth and increases one's lifespan.

When Jesus son of Mary (peace be upon them both) passed by the shore of the sea, he threw a morsel from his provisions into the water. Some of the disciples said to him: 'O Spirit of God and His Word! Why did you do that, when it was from your own provisions?' He said: 'I did that for an animal from among the animals of the water to eat, and its reward with God is great.'

key_terms.الدُّقَّةُ: Fine seasoning; specifically salt mixed with other spices — the humblest and most basic of condiments, used here to indicate what the Imam would have shared even with non-followers
key_terms.خَازِنٌ: Treasurer/keeper — a divine guardian appointed over every created thing; charity alone has no such intermediary as God Himself oversees it
key_terms.رُوحَ اللَّهِ: Spirit of God — a Quranic title for Jesus (AS), affirming his exalted but created status
key_terms.صَدَقَةَ اللَّيْلِ: Night charity — given in darkness to preserve the giver's anonymity; it has special spiritual merit
key_terms.ظُلَّةَ بَنِي سَاعِدَةَ: The canopy/shelter of Banu Sa'ida — a covered meeting place in Medina where the Ansar gathered; it was here that the dispute over the caliphate took place after the Prophet's death
key_terms.كَلِمَتَهُ: His Word — another Quranic title for Jesus, referring to God's command 'Be' that created him

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the virtue of giving charity at night?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates an incident in which Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) secretly went out at night during drizzle to personally distribute bread to sleeping people at the shelter of Banu Sa'ida — even those who did not follow the truth — demonstrating the universality of charity. The Imam then teaches that God personally oversees charity (unlike all other created things, which have a treasurer/keeper), that his own father would kiss and smell charity before giving it out of reverence, that night charity extinguishes divine anger and day charity increases wealth and lifespan, and that even Jesus threw food into the sea for a sea creature, earning great reward. The hadith addresses Mu'alla ibn Khunays, the Imam's trusted agent in Medina, who witnessed this act of nocturnal generosity and recorded these teachings.
word_analysis: we would have shared with them

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Sa’dan Bin Muslim, from Moalla Bin Khunays who said, 
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> went out during a night and it had drizzled, and he<sup>asws</sup> was intending (to go to) a canopy of the Clan of Saeeda, so I followed him<sup>asws</sup>, and there was something which had dropped off from him<sup>asws</sup>. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, Return it to us<sup>asws</sup>’. 
He (the narrator) said, ‘So I followed him<sup>asws</sup> and greeted him<sup>asws</sup>. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Moalla?’ I said, ‘Yes, may I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Seek with your hands, so whatever you find from anything, hand it over to me<sup>asws</sup>’. I found a lot of pieces of bread, and I went on handing these over to him<sup>asws</sup>, whatever I found. So then I was with a basket of bread which I was frustrated from carrying it, so I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! Carry it upon my head’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, I<sup>asws</sup> am first with it than you are, but come with me<sup>asws</sup>’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘So we came over to a canopy of the Clan of Saeeda, and we were with a group of people sleeping. So he<sup>asws</sup> went on to tuck the bread, and two breads until he<sup>asws</sup> came to the last of them. Then we left, so I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! Do they recognise the Truth?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said, ‘If they had recognised it, I<sup>asws</sup> would have consoled them with the delicacy, and the delicacy, it is the salt.

Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Blessed and High did not Create anything except there is a treasurer for it treasuring it, except for the charity, for the Lord<sup>azwj</sup> Pursues it by Himself<sup>saww</sup>, and my<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup>, when he<sup>asws</sup> gave something in charity, would place it in the hand of the beggar, then retract from it, so he<sup>asws</sup> would kiss it, and smell it, then return it in the hand of the beggar. A charity at night extinguishes the Anger of the Lord<sup>azwj</sup>, and obliterates the major sins, and makes the Reckoning easier; and the charity by the day yields the wealth and increases in the life span.

Isa Bin Maryam<sup>as</sup>, when he<sup>as</sup> passed upon the coast of the sea, threw a bite from his<sup>as</sup> provision into the water. So one of the disciples said to him<sup>as</sup>, ‘O Spirit of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and His<sup>azwj</sup> Speech! Why did you<sup>as</sup> do this, and rather it is your<sup>as</sup> provision?’ So he<sup>as</sup> said: ‘I<sup>as</sup> did this for an animal from animals of the water to eat from it, and its Reward in the Presence of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, is great’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Khalid from Sa‘dan ibn Muslim from Mu ’alia ibn Khunays who has said the following: “One rainy night, abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, went out to Zullah of banu Sa‘idah. I followed him and saw that some of his things fell down. He said, ‘Bismi Allah (by the name of Allah). O Lord, please return it back to us.’ I went to him and greeted him with the greetings of peace. He said, ‘Is it you, Mu‘alla’?’ I replied, ‘Yes, may Allah keep my soul in the service of your cause.’ He said. ‘Search with your hands and give us whatever you find.’ I found a great deal of bread spread around and kept giving whatever bread I found to him. I found a sack full of bread so heavy that I could not lift it up. I then said, ‘May Allah keep my soul in the service of your cause; allow me to pick it up on my head.’ He said, ‘No, I am more proper for this than you are, but come along with me.’

We then reached Zullah of banu Sa‘idah and found a whole company of people sleeping. He then began to make one or two breads available to each one to the last of them, in a way that no one else could see. We then returned and I asked, ‘May Allah keep my soul in the service of your cause, do these people know the truth (are they Shi‘a)?’ He replied, ‘Were they of those who know the truth, we would have joined them for bread with salt.

Allah, the most Blessed, the most High, has made a treasurer for everything He has created, except charity. The Lord Himself is the treasurer thereof. When my father would give charity, he would place it in the hand of the person asking for help, then take it back from him, kiss and smell it, and then give it back to him. Giving charity during the night extinguishes the anger of the Lord, deletes the great sin and makes presentation of one’s accounts easier. Giving charity during the day increases one’s wealth and longevity of life.

Jesus, son of Mary, when passing by the coastline of the ocean, threw a loaf of bread in the water. Someone among his disciples said, ‘O the Spirit and Word of Allah, why did you throw your bread in the water, it was your food for the day?’ Jesus replied, ‘I did it for the living things in the ocean that may eat it and the reward for it with Allah is great.’”
